findings.reason: shadowSupersession starts one `git merge-base --is-ancestor` process for every ordered pair of distinct tips, n·(n−1) processes, 4 at a time, on every GET /api/git/shadows. The list filter already costs 2 processes per ref. With 30 shadows that is 870 extra git spawns per read of the list, which the Releases screen and GitStatusBadge refetch. The same answer takes about n+1 git calls: `git merge-base --independent <tips…>` returns the terminal tips in one call, then a `git for-each-ref --contains <tip>` (or one `rev-list` walk) per non-terminal tip gives the terminals above it. Not a bug, but the cost grows quadratically with the number of Runs on a read-only endpoint.

resolveShadow now always runs the whole list filter (filteredShadowsAt: merge-base plus diff for every ref under refs/runs/) and the quadratic supersession scan. None of its three callers reads `supersededBy`: release-shadow-diff.ts:165, release-accept-shadow.ts:269 and run-read.ts:378. run-read.ts:378 already ran listShadows() just before, so that path does the scan twice. Every shadow diff, Accept and run-read therefore pays the full list cost for a field it throws away. Consider computing supersession only when asked (an option flag, or a separate method) so these hot paths keep their old cost.
